28.summary: Validate broker authorization, account isolation and real authentication in one bounded live-guest history, with shared account setup and final owned cleanup.
steps: Prepare the fixture accounts and real caller connections, then check the declared child, parent, kiosk and locked-administrator permissions for discovery, own-account lookup, preferences, applications, time, sessions, requests, policy management and diagnostics.
Attempt cross-child reads and writes, direct private-record access and diagnostic impersonation; compare state after each refusal and check sorted eligible child and approver discovery.
Create disposable child and approver identities, remember their selections, delete each identity and retry discovery and stale selections on existing connections.
Exercise the declared root management permissions, request-only refusals, root approver exclusion and diagnostic component restrictions, then restore the selected child's original settings.

Check noninteractive and system callers, ineligible child targets and approvers on both request surfaces; try an enabled child request without an agent, and set and clear authoritative child and parent icons.
Independently vary administrator interactive-shell and safe-name eligibility while retaining valid role, locality, system-account and lock predicates; try discovery and direct approval selection.
Prepare real LDAP child and administrator identities, verify their nonlocal status, try discovery and caller/target/approver operations, then restore the owned directory fixture.
Change one child's controls and request choices while comparing other accounts; change parent and child roles on persistent connections, test immediate authority loss and restore each role.
On both child and kiosk surfaces, disconnect a requester while approval is pending, verify cancellation and unchanged state, then authenticate a fresh request and revoke the resulting grant.

On both request surfaces, delete a disposable child while the real parent authentication prompt is pending, finish authentication and verify the original requester connection and surviving account state.
For the child request surface, independently change the target child's role and the selected parent's role during authentication; finish authentication and restore each mutation.
For the kiosk request surface, independently change the target child's role and saved request preferences during authentication; finish authentication and restore each mutation.
Begin a child request, lock its selected parent while authentication is pending, retry discovery and authentication, then restore the parent's lock state and original child settings.
Repeat the pending-authentication parent-lock refusal from the kiosk request surface with independent state observations and restoration.

From the child surface, try the wrong parent's password and then the selected parent's password; observe the real grant, test that the requester gained no account or policy-management authority, and restore controls.
Repeat selected-parent password validation and post-approval authority checks from the kiosk surface, then collect results and finish owned VM restoration and cleanup.
expected: Role permissions match every declared method/role cell: child discovery is refused, eligible managers can discover children, only a child can identify or prepare its own session, eligible preference/time/request-choice operations succeed, application listing and policy management remain parent-only, disabled or agentless requests grant no time, and each role may log only its own component. Locked administrators retain the declared management and diagnostic permissions.

Cross-child reads and writes are denied without changing the other child's preferences; private records remain unreadable and unwritable to child, parent and kiosk callers; diagnostic impersonation is denied, and discovery returns sorted eligible identities with empty or absolute icon paths.
Deleted identities disappear from discovery immediately; stale child and approver selections return InvalidRequest without recreating deleted records or changing surviving accounts.

Root's allowed management calls apply their requested changes, its request-only operations and foreign-component logging are denied, UID zero is never offered or accepted as an approver, and unrelated accounts remain unchanged.

Both ineligible caller classes and every declared invalid target or approver are denied without account-state changes; an agentless enabled-child request grants zero time; returned child and parent icons exactly match their authoritative set or cleared values.

A valid interactive administrator is discoverable as the positive control; independently noninteractive or unsafe-name administrators are excluded from discovery and direct selection on both surfaces without changing account state.

Real LDAP identities are otherwise eligible but nonlocal; both are excluded from discovery and all declared remote caller, target and approver operations are denied without changing local account state.

Management changes affect only the selected child. Existing parent and child connections immediately lose their previous authority after role changes, preserve policy state and recover after exact role restoration.

Requester loss cancels the pending approval without reaching the write pipeline or granting time; the authentication agent survives, the transaction is released, and a fresh authenticated connection can receive a grant independently.

Both authenticated requests reject the deleted target with InvalidRequest while their original bus connections remain owned by the requester; no deleted record is recreated and all surviving account state is preserved.
Child-surface requests authenticated against stale target or approver roles are denied without granting time or writing account state; each exact role mutation is restored.
Kiosk requests authenticated against a stale child role or changed preferences are denied without granting time or writing account state; each exact mutation is restored.
The parent locked during a child request disappears from approver discovery and cannot authenticate a grant; account state is unchanged and the original lock state and child settings are restored.
The same pending-lock boundary holds independently for kiosk requests: no grant or account-state change occurs and original settings are restored.
Only the selected parent's password approves the child request and creates a real positive grant; approval gives the child no account-role or policy-management authority and preserves other accounts.

Only the selected parent's password approves the kiosk request and creates a real positive grant; approval gives the kiosk no account-role or policy-management authority, preserves other accounts, and the attempt completes its owned restoration and cleanup before completion is published.

267.summary: Validate installed kiosk integration, native application policy, probe recovery and offline expiry enforcement in one prepared live guest, with final owned restoration and cleanup.
steps: Prepare the enforcement fixtures; inspect the request-station account and selected session, exercise real PAM login admission and refusal, and check ordinary users' shared desktop integration.

Apply and clear hard and soft command policies for one child, repeat independently for executable paths containing whitespace, then switch the selected child's application catalogue and check scoped launchers.
Refuse native probe admission and retry a fresh generation; exercise broker storage lifetime and sandbox restrictions, permanently lose a sender, then complete another fresh generation.

Apply a versioned application pattern, add and trust a new matching version, clear the block and restore policy; independently remove another application's menu launcher while retaining its executable, save the unchanged block, test launches, clear it and restore policy.

Recover extension controls while the child is logged out, exercise failed activation and rollback, check graphical and terminal PAM time-limit scopes, then collect results and finish owned VM restoration and cleanup.
expected: The dedicated session and graphical admission gates are correctly configured, alternate-login admission is refused, saved routing is preserved and kiosk integration leaves ordinary users' services and applications unaffected.

Command and whitespace-path policies block only the selected child in every declared hard/soft and screen-time state; clearing blocks restores access, other accounts' policies remain unchanged and each child's catalogue resolves its own launchers and overrides.

Refused and disconnected probes settle safely; fresh generations succeed independently after refusal and sender loss, probe storage survives the declared service lifecycle and execution respects the installed broker sandbox.

Initial and newly trusted matching versions remain blocked only for the selected child without changing active pattern rules. A missing launcher disappears from the catalogue but its saved block still denies executable launches after an unchanged save. Clearing either block restores access and each independent history restores its exact original policy.

Offline recovery preserves extension choices and other accounts; failed activation and rollback do not grant access, time enforcement follows each login type, and the attempt completes owned restoration and cleanup before completion is published.

295.summary: Validate automatic extension monitoring, session and broker lifecycle, private diagnostics, Parent controls and authenticated kiosk recovery in five finite stages on one prepared child desktop, with shared setup and owned cleanup.
steps: Prepare the monitor desktop; begin with the extension never loaded, enable control, repeatedly disable the extension individually and through GNOME's global switch, allow a healthy quiet interval, then turn parental control off.
Exercise fresh child session, bus and shell identities; defer recovery across lock and approval activity, cancel the pending prompt, then stop and restart the broker with controls saved off.

Cause a native extension error while its report window cannot open, restore the display and edit the report draft, repeat failures across broker restart, exercise session-bus loss and explicit recovery, then interrupt the child session after recovery.
Use Parent with an enabled child's extension disabled, switch to another enabled child, select a child with saved-off controls, then enable controls while GNOME's global extension switch is disabled.

Authenticate one real kiosk request while the child's extension and global switch are disabled, observe the grant and attributed extension recovery, repeat only the idempotent recovery check, then finish owned result collection, restoration and cleanup.
expected: Monitoring restores the extension from the never-loaded state and repeated individual/global disablement at a bounded rate, resumes promptly after quiet, preserves policies and unrelated extension choices, and respects the parent's saved-off state.

Native extension failure is reported through one private report whose edited draft survives repeated errors and broker restart without automatic submission; unsafe retries stop on bus or session loss, exact fixture bytes are restored and explicit recovery restores healthy monitoring.

Each eligible Parent action owns its native extension recovery and preserves unrelated settings; merely selecting saved-off controls leaves them off, while first enablement recovers the extension/global switch, applies the daily limit and clears the stale grant.
